title: Diploma programme admission requirements, 2027 intake
text: These requirements apply to all two-year and three-year diploma programmes starting in September 2027 or January 2028. Applicants need a high school diploma or an equivalent such as a high school equivalency certificate, with an overall average of at least 62 percent in their top six Grade 12 courses. Grade 12 English with a final grade of 60 percent or higher is required for every diploma. Additional course requirements by programme: Civil Engineering Technology, Electrical Engineering Technology and Computer Systems Technology need Grade 12 mathematics (any stream) at 60 percent or higher. The Practical Nursing diploma needs Grade 12 Biology at 65 percent or higher and Grade 11 Chemistry at 60 percent or higher, and admitted students must provide a vulnerable sector police check dated within 6 months before the first clinical placement. Business Administration, Culinary Arts and Early Childhood Education have no additional course requirements, although Early Childhood Education students also need a vulnerable sector police check. Applicants who are missing one required course can be given a conditional offer if they complete the Institute's free Academic Upgrading module for that subject before 15 August. Current Grade 12 students are assessed on their midterm or Grade 11 final grades and receive a conditional offer; the final transcript must reach the admissions office by 15 July. The Practical Nursing diploma admits 48 students per year at the Fallowmere campus only.

title: Bachelor's degree admission requirements, 2027 intake
text: These requirements apply to the four-year applied degrees starting in September 2027: the Bachelor of Applied Technology in Construction Management, the Bachelor of Business Administration (Applied), and the Bachelor of Applied Science in Environmental Monitoring. Degree programmes start in September only; there is no January intake. Applicants need a high school diploma with an overall average of at least 72 percent in their top six Grade 12 courses, and Grade 12 English at 65 percent or higher. Construction Management and Environmental Monitoring also need Grade 12 pre-calculus mathematics at 65 percent or higher; Environmental Monitoring also needs one Grade 12 science (Biology, Chemistry or Physics) at 65 percent or higher. Business Administration (Applied) needs Grade 12 mathematics in any stream at 60 percent or higher. Unlike diploma programmes, degree programmes do not give conditional offers to applicants who are missing a required course; the course must be completed before the application deadline. Graduates of a related two-year diploma from the Institute with a cumulative GPA of 3.0 or higher can enter the third year of the matching degree directly through a bridging term held in May and June. Graduates of related diplomas from other colleges are assessed course by course for transfer credit instead.

title: Application fees and deadlines, 2027-28 intakes
text: These rules apply to applications for September 2027 and January 2028 and replace the 2026-27 application rules. The application fee is $85 for domestic applicants and $150 for international applicants. It is non-refundable and covers up to three programme choices on one application; choices can be changed free of charge until an offer is made. Degree programmes and the Practical Nursing diploma have a fixed deadline of 1 February 2027 for September; complete applications received by that date are given equal consideration, and later applications are considered only if seats remain after the first round of offers on 15 March. All other diploma programmes use rolling admission: files are assessed in the order they are completed, a decision is sent within 4 weeks of a complete file, and programmes close when full. International applicants for any September programme must apply by 1 May 2027 so there is time to obtain a study permit; for January 2028 the international deadline is 15 September 2027 and the domestic deadline is 1 November 2027. January intakes are offered for diploma programmes only. Applicants who were refused in the previous cycle may reapply once at a reduced fee of $25.

title: Application fees and deadlines, 2026-27 intakes (superseded)
text: Status: superseded on 1 October 2026 by the application rules for the 2027-28 intakes; kept for reference for applications made under the old rules. For September 2026 and January 2027 the application fee was $75 for domestic applicants and $125 for international applicants, non-refundable, and each application covered one programme choice only; a second choice needed a second fee. Degree programmes had a fixed deadline of 15 February 2026. All diploma programmes, including Practical Nursing, used rolling admission and stayed open until full. International applicants for September had to apply by 15 May 2026. Decisions on complete diploma files were sent within 6 weeks. There was no reduced reapplication fee. Applications submitted before 1 October 2026 for the January 2027 intake continue to be processed under these rules, including the one-choice limit.

title: English language proficiency requirements, effective 1 September 2026
text: This policy applies to all applications received from 1 September 2026 and replaces the English language requirements issued in March 2024. Applicants whose first language is not English must show English proficiency unless they completed at least three consecutive years of full-time study in English in a country where English is the main language, ending no more than five years before the programme start date. Approved academic English tests scored on a nine-band scale: diploma programmes need an overall score of 5.5 with no band below 5.0; degree programmes and the Practical Nursing diploma need 6.5 overall with no band below 6.0. For approved internet-based tests scored out of 120, diploma programmes need 60 and degree and Practical Nursing programmes need 84. Applicants may also sit the Institute's own English Placement Assessment on campus or online for a fee of $60; its result is valid only for admission to the Institute. Test results are accepted if the test was taken no more than three years before the application date. Band scores from two sittings of the same approved test taken within six months of each other may be combined, using the best score in each band, to meet the requirement. Applicants who narrowly miss the requirement may be offered a place with the 12-week English Pathway term starting in May.

title: English language requirements, March 2024 (superseded)
text: Status: superseded by the English language proficiency requirements effective 1 September 2026, and kept for applicants assessed before that date. Under the March 2024 rules, diploma programmes required an overall score of 6.0 on an approved academic nine-band test with no band below 5.5, and degree programmes required 6.5 with no band below 6.0. Internet-based test minimums were 70 for diplomas and 84 for degrees. Test results were valid for two years from the test date, and every band score had to come from a single sitting; scores from different sittings could not be combined. The exemption for study in English required four years of full-time study in an English-speaking country. There was no in-house English Placement Assessment and no English Pathway term; applicants who missed the requirement were refused and asked to reapply with new scores.

title: Accepting an offer: confirmation deposit and deferral (domestic applicants)
text: Domestic applicants accept an offer by paying a confirmation deposit of $500 within 30 days of the offer date; if the deposit is not received, the seat is released to the next applicant. The deposit is credited in full to first-term tuition. It is fully refundable if you withdraw your acceptance in writing before 1 July for a September start or before 1 November for a January start; after those dates it is non-refundable. Offers to diploma programmes cannot be deferred. An applicant who wants to start in a later intake must decline the offer and reapply, paying the application fee again, and admission is not guaranteed. Offers to degree programmes can be deferred once, for up to 12 months, if the request is made before 15 August; the deposit is carried over and the original admission average is used. Entrance scholarships are not carried over when a degree offer is deferred; the applicant is reassessed in the year they start. International applicants should see the international admissions page for tuition deposit rules, which differ.

title: International applicants: transcripts, tuition deposit and letter of acceptance
text: International applicants upload copies of their secondary or post-secondary transcripts with the application, and if documents are not in English, a certified English translation must be attached. The Institute evaluates all international credentials in-house, free of charge; a credential evaluation report from an outside agency is not required and is not used for admission. Decisions are normally sent within 3 to 6 weeks of a complete file. To accept an offer, international applicants pay a tuition deposit of $6,000, which is credited to first-term tuition. The official letter of acceptance needed for a study permit application is issued within 10 business days after the deposit clears. The deposit is refunded less a $500 administration fee if the study permit is refused and the refusal letter is sent to the Institute before the end of the second week of classes; otherwise it is non-refundable once the letter of acceptance has been issued. If the study permit has not been approved in time, an international student may defer once to the next intake of the same programme at no cost, including diploma programmes, and the deposit is held. International students must be in Canada and attend classes by the end of the second week of term, or their registration is cancelled.

title: Tuition fees and instalment plans, 2027-28
text: Annual tuition for 2027-28, covering the fall and winter terms: domestic diploma programmes $4,380; domestic degree programmes $6,950; international diploma programmes $16,800; international degree programmes $19,400. Practical Nursing carries an additional clinical fee of $650 per year. Ancillary fees of $1,120 per year cover the student association, the town transit pass and the health and dental plan; students with equivalent coverage may opt out of the health and dental part ($310) by 20 September. Fall term fees are due 15 August and winter term fees are due 10 December. Domestic students may pay each term in three instalments, at registration, on 15 October and on 15 November for fall (or at registration, 15 February and 15 March for winter), for a plan fee of $40 per term; no interest is charged. International students pay their first term in full through the tuition deposit and the balance due 15 August, and may use the instalment plan from their second term onward. A late payment fee of $75 per term applies to any missed due date or instalment, and a registration hold blocks timetable and transcript access until the balance is paid.

title: Withdrawal and tuition refund schedule
text: Students who withdraw from their programme must submit the withdrawal form in the student portal; the date the form is submitted is the withdrawal date used for refunds. Stopping attendance or not paying is not a withdrawal and does not reduce fees owed. Refunds of tuition for a term, other than the non-refundable part of any deposit, are calculated as follows. Withdrawal before the first day of classes: 100 percent. During the first week of classes: 70 percent. During the second week: 50 percent. During the third week: 25 percent. From the fourth week onward: no refund. Ancillary fees are refunded in full up to the end of the second week and not after. The Practical Nursing clinical fee is non-refundable once the first placement has started. Weeks are counted from the first scheduled day of classes in the term, not from the student's first class. International students who withdraw after classes begin receive the same percentages, and the Institute is required to report the withdrawal to immigration authorities. Refunds are paid to the original payment method within 30 days.

title: Entrance scholarships and bursaries, 2027 intake
text: Entrance scholarships are awarded automatically to domestic applicants based on the admission average used for their offer; no separate application is needed. An average of 85 to 89.9 percent receives $1,500 and an average of 90 percent or higher receives $2,500. International applicants with an equivalent average of 80 percent or higher automatically receive an International Entrance Award of $2,000. Awards are applied as a tuition credit, half in the fall term and half in the winter term, and the student must be enrolled full time in the first year. Entrance scholarships are not renewable. Bursaries are based on financial need and require an application in the student portal. The fall bursary window runs from 1 September to 30 September and the winter window from 15 January to 5 February. Bursaries are up to $1,200 per term. Domestic students must have applied for provincial student aid before applying for a bursary; international students can apply for the International Student Emergency Bursary of up to $800 once per year. Bursary results are released within three weeks of the window closing.

title: Transfer credit and prior learning assessment
text: Transfer credit is granted for courses completed at a recognised post-secondary institution with a grade of C (60 percent) or higher, where the course matches at least 75 percent of the learning outcomes of an Institute course. Programme-specific courses must have been completed within the last 7 years; general education courses such as English, psychology or sociology are accepted within the last 10 years. There is no fee for a transfer credit assessment. Requests must be made through the student portal by the end of the second week of the term in which the course is scheduled. Prior learning assessment and recognition covers learning from work and life experience. It is done by challenge exam or by portfolio, and the fee is $120 per course, payable before the assessment is booked and not refundable if the assessment is unsuccessful. Each course can be challenged once. Combined transfer credit and prior learning credit cannot exceed 50 percent of a programme's credits; at least half must be completed at the Institute to receive the credential. Practical Nursing clinical placements cannot be challenged.

title: Residence: application, rates and campuses, 2027-28
text: Residence applications open in the student portal once you accept your offer of admission. A residence deposit of $300 is required with the application and is applied to the first term's residence fee; it is refundable less $50 if you cancel before 15 June. First-year students who apply by 1 June are guaranteed a room at the Fallowmere campus; later applicants are placed in order of application as rooms become free. Fallowmere has two halls, Riverside Hall and Quarry Hall. Rates per term are $3,100 for a shared double room and $3,950 for a single room, and a meal plan of $1,700 per term is mandatory for all Fallowmere residents. The Pine Hollow campus has 60 single rooms in Larch House at $3,300 per term with shared kitchens and no meal plan, available only to students whose programme is taught at Pine Hollow. Residence agreements are signed one term at a time, not for the full academic year: a student who gives written notice by 15 November can leave at the end of the fall term and owes nothing for winter. Residents moving in for fall can arrive from 30 August; residences stay open over the winter break for a fee of $20 per night.

title: Mature applicant entry, conditional offers and admission appeals
text: Applicants who do not have a high school diploma can apply as mature applicants to diploma programmes if they will be at least 20 years old by the first day of classes and have been out of full-time secondary school for at least one year. Mature applicants complete an academic placement assessment in English and mathematics, which costs $45 and can be taken once every 30 days; the result replaces the Grade 12 course requirements for most diplomas. Mature entry is not available for degree programmes or for the Practical Nursing diploma, which require the listed courses. Conditional offers are withdrawn if final grades are below the required level or the final transcript is not received by 15 July. Applicants who are refused or whose offer is withdrawn may request a reconsideration within 10 business days of the decision. Requests are made in writing to the Registrar with a $40 fee, which is refunded if the decision is changed. Reconsideration is only granted for a procedural error in the assessment or for new information, such as updated grades, that was not available at the time of the decision. A decision is given within 15 business days and is final.

title: Orientation dates, admissions office hours and campus visits
text: Fall 2027 orientation: international students attend a mandatory international orientation on Wednesday 1 and Thursday 2 September 2027, and all new students attend New Student Day on Friday 3 September. Classes begin on Tuesday 7 September 2027, after Labour Day. Winter 2028 orientation is on Thursday 6 January 2028 and classes begin Monday 10 January. Students who miss New Student Day must complete the online orientation module before the end of the first week. The admissions office is in Room 140 of the Student Services Building at the Fallowmere campus and is open Monday to Friday, 8:30 am to 4:30 pm, with extended hours until 7 pm on Thursdays from February to August. It is closed on weekends and statutory holidays. The Pine Hollow campus admissions desk is open Tuesdays and Thursdays only, 10 am to 3 pm. The admissions line is 1-888-555-0142. Guided campus tours run at 10 am on Saturdays in October and March at Fallowmere and must be booked at least 48 hours ahead; self-guided tour maps are available at the front desk on weekdays.
